meta.titre: Computer Ergonomics: health problems and how to prevent them
meta.sous_theme: Health risks of computer use and safe workstation habits

source.epreuve_titre: GCE O/L Computer Science past paper (Cameroon)

sections.contenu_markdown: Many pupils in Limbe and Douala now spend hours at a computer or a phone: typing homework, playing games or following lessons. After a long session the eyes burn, the neck hurts and the wrists feel tired. The GCE regularly asks you to name the health problems linked to computer use and to say how each one can be prevented. A good answer pairs each problem with a measure that really fits it.

items: A monitor is the screen on which a computer displays its output.
The keyboard and the mouse are used for long periods of typing and clicking.
Posture means the way in which the body is held when sitting or standing.

sections.titre: Ergonomics: health problems of computer use and their prevention
sections.contenu_markdown:
### What ergonomics means

**Ergonomics** is the study of how to design equipment and the working place so that they fit the user. A good ergonomic set-up protects health, reduces tiredness and lets the user work faster and more comfortably.

### Health problems, causes and prevention

| Problem | Typical signs | Main cause | Prevention |
|---|---|---|---|
| **RSI** (Repetitive Strain Injury) | Pain, tingling or numbness in the wrists, hands and fingers | Repeating the same small movements (typing, clicking) for a long time | Take regular short breaks and stretch, keep the wrists straight with a wrist rest, use an ergonomic keyboard or mouse |
| **CVS** (Computer Vision Syndrome, or digital eye strain) | Tired, dry or blurred eyes, headaches | Looking at a screen for a long time, glare, poor lighting | Look away from the screen at regular intervals, use an anti-glare filter, adjust brightness and contrast, light the room well |
| **Back and neck pain** | Aching back, stiff neck and shoulders | Bad posture, a chair without support, a screen that is too low | Use an adjustable chair with back support, keep the feet flat on the floor, put the top of the screen at eye level, walk around regularly |
| **Radiation** | Concern about exposure to radiation from the screen | Older CRT monitors emit more radiation than flat screens | Use an LCD or LED screen and sit at a comfortable distance from it |
| **Stress and fatigue** | Headaches, bad mood, loss of concentration | Long hours without rest, noise, poor lighting | Plan breaks, work in a quiet, well-lit room |

### Safety around the equipment

Keep cables tidy so that nobody trips, do not overload a power socket, keep drinks away from the computer and make sure the room has enough fresh air.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When the question says 'state' a problem and 'describe' or 'give' a measure
variantes.contenu_markdown: Write each problem on its own line with the measure next to it. The measure must match the problem: breaks and stretching for RSI, looking away and an anti-glare filter for CVS. State the problem by its name, not by its cause.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When the question says 'describe how a user should sit' or 'advise on the arrangement'
variantes.contenu_markdown: Go through the body from top to bottom and give one instruction with its reason: screen at eye level and an arm's length away (eyes and neck), back against the chair (spine), feet flat on the floor (legs), forearms level with the keyboard and wrists straight (hands), and light that does not shine on the screen (glare).

variantes.quand_utiliser: When the question asks which hardware is safer or emits more radiation
variantes.contenu_markdown: A CRT monitor is large, heavy and emits more radiation than an LCD or LED screen, and some CRT screens flicker. An LCD or LED screen is thin and light, uses less power and emits less radiation. For this reason a flat screen is the better choice for people who work long hours.

sections.enonce_markdown: The head teacher of a secondary school in Limbe is preparing a new computer room for pupils. As the ICT teacher, advise the pupils on how to sit and how to arrange the equipment so that they avoid health problems. (6 marks)

etapes.action: Read the command word and the mark allocation.
etapes.justification: 'Advise' asks for clear instructions, and 6 marks means about six separate points, each with a reason.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Plan for six instructions, each with a short reason.

etapes.action: Build a plan by part of the body and the environment.
etapes.justification: A plan from top to bottom covers every health problem and avoids repeating a point.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Eyes, neck, back, feet, wrists, lighting.

etapes.action: Write each instruction with its reason.
etapes.justification: A bare instruction earns less than an instruction that is explained.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Screen at eye level and an arm's length away: protects the eyes and the neck.

etapes.action: Add the instructions for the back, the hands and the room.
etapes.justification: These cover back pain, RSI and glare.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Back against the chair, feet flat, wrists straight, no light shining on the screen.

etapes.action: Finish with the habit of taking breaks.
etapes.justification: Even a perfect set-up does not prevent harm if the user never stops.
etapes.resultat_markdown: A short break and a stretch regularly.

sections.conclusion_markdown:
Model answer (one mark per point):

1. Place the top of the screen at eye level and about an arm's length away, to protect the eyes and the neck.
2. Sit with the back against a chair that supports it, to prevent back pain.
3. Keep both feet flat on the floor, so that the legs and the lower back are not strained.
4. Keep the forearms level with the keyboard and the wrists straight, with a wrist rest if needed, to prevent RSI.
5. Place the screen so that no window or lamp shines on it, or use an anti-glare filter, to avoid glare and eye strain (CVS).
6. Take a short break and stretch at regular intervals, and look away from the screen, to rest the eyes and the hands.

items.erreur_markdown: A student writes 'using the computer for many hours' as a health problem.
items.pourquoi_faux: This is a cause, not a health problem. The question asks for the harm to the user.
items.correction_markdown: Name the problem: for example **eye strain (CVS)** or **RSI**, and then give the cause if the question needs it.

items.erreur_markdown: A student writes 'To prevent RSI, use an anti-glare filter.'
items.pourquoi_faux: An anti-glare filter reduces reflections on the screen, so it helps the eyes. RSI affects the wrists and hands and is caused by repeated movements.
items.correction_markdown: For RSI: take regular breaks and stretch, keep the wrists straight, use a wrist rest. The anti-glare filter belongs to CVS.

items.erreur_markdown: A student writes that RSI is 'damage to the eyes caused by the screen'.
items.pourquoi_faux: The eyes are affected by CVS. RSI is an injury to muscles and tendons caused by repeated movements, mainly in the wrists, hands and fingers.
items.correction_markdown: RSI = Repetitive Strain Injury (hands and wrists). CVS = Computer Vision Syndrome (eyes).

items.erreur_markdown: A student answers 'Sit properly.' to a question on how to avoid back pain.
items.pourquoi_faux: The answer is too vague to earn marks. The examiner needs a precise action.
items.correction_markdown: 'Sit with the back against the chair, with the feet flat on the floor, and keep the screen at eye level.'

items.erreur_markdown: A student advises: 'Sit as close as possible to the screen so that you can read well.'
items.pourquoi_faux: Sitting too close tires the eyes and exposes the user to more radiation from an older screen.
items.correction_markdown: Sit about an arm's length from the screen and increase the text size if needed.

items.enonce_markdown: Match each problem to the part of the body that it mainly affects: RSI, CVS, back pain. Choose from: the eyes, the spine, the wrists and hands.
items.solution_markdown: RSI affects **the wrists and hands**. CVS affects **the eyes**. Back pain affects **the spine** (back and neck).

items.enonce_markdown:
After three hours of typing practice, a pupil has tingling in the wrist and tired, dry eyes.

(a) Name the problem that each sign points to.

(b) Give two measures that would have prevented each problem.
items.solution_markdown:
(a) The tingling wrist points to **RSI**. The tired, dry eyes point to **CVS**.

(b) RSI: take a short break and stretch the hands regularly; keep the wrists straight, with a wrist rest or an ergonomic keyboard.

CVS: look away from the screen at regular intervals; use an anti-glare filter or adjust the brightness, and light the room so that nothing reflects on the screen.

items.enonce_markdown:
A school has some old CRT monitors and some LCD monitors in the same room.

(a) Give two reasons why the LCD monitors are better for the health of the pupils.

(b) Suggest two rules that the teacher should put on the wall of the computer room.
items.solution_markdown:
(a) Any two: an LCD screen emits **less radiation** than a CRT; it does not flicker in the way some CRT screens do, so it tires the eyes less; it is thin and light and uses less power, so it is easier to place at the right height.

(b) Any two sensible rules, for example: **take a break from the screen at regular intervals**; **sit upright, with the back against the chair and the feet flat on the floor**; **no drinks near the computers**; **keep cables tidy so that nobody trips**.

items_markdown: Ergonomics is the study of designing equipment and the workplace to fit the user.
RSI (Repetitive Strain Injury) affects the wrists and hands; CVS (Computer Vision Syndrome) affects the eyes; poor posture causes back and neck pain.
Match every measure to its problem: breaks and stretching for RSI, looking away and an anti-glare filter for CVS, a supportive chair and a screen at eye level for the back and neck.
CRT monitors emit more radiation than LCD or LED screens.
Give precise actions, not vague advice such as 'sit properly'.
